```text
1	# Linux GUI Apps — packaging mechanisms, this repo's strategy, and how to add a new one
2	
3	Ubuntu has **five** packaging mechanisms for desktop apps. They differ in
4	*where binaries land*, *whether anything keeps them current*, and *how
5	desktop integration (icon, `.desktop`, MIME handlers) gets wired up*.
6	
7	This doc:
8	
9	1. lays out the five mechanisms and the trade-off matrix,
10	2. inventories every GUI app this repo's `gui_apps_linux` ansible role
11	   knows about (plus the snaps you probably installed via Ubuntu App
12	   Center), so you can tell at a glance which path each app is on,
13	3. gives a decision tree for adding a *new* app to the role.
14	
15	## TL;DR — five mechanisms, one trade-off matrix
16	
17	| Mechanism | Auto-update? | Install scope | Desktop integration | Sandbox |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| **`.deb` w/ apt-source postinst** | ✅ via `apt upgrade` | system-wide (`/usr/share/...`) | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
20	| **`.deb` w/o apt-source postinst** | ❌ manual re-deploy | system-wide | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
21	| **Snap** (Ubuntu App Center) | ✅ `snapd` background daemon | `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
22	| **Flatpak** (Flathub) | ✅ `flatpak update` | per-user `~/.var/app/...` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
23	| **AppImage + AppImageLauncher** | ❌ re-download | per-user `~/Applications/` | ✅ via AIL daemon | ❌ |
24	| Cargo / from source | ❌ via `cargo install --force` | per-user `~/.cargo/bin/` | ❌ manual `.desktop` | ❌ |
25	| Tarball / `.tar.xz` | ❌ pure manual | per-user (anywhere) | ❌ manual | ❌ |
26	
27	The **green-checkmark `.deb` row is the gold standard** when upstream
28	provides it. Snap and Flatpak are the auto-update fallbacks for vendors
29	who don't ship `.deb` (or who want sandboxing). AppImage is the
30	last-mile bridge for everyone else.
31	
32	## Priority order on Ubuntu
33	
34	The matrix above is *what each mechanism does*. The list below is *which
35	to pick when you have a choice* — the explicit ordering this repo
36	follows when a vendor ships in multiple formats:
37	
38	1. **`.deb` w/ auto apt-source** — `apt upgrade` keeps it current with zero
39	   sandbox overhead and native startup speed. The right answer for
40	   hot-path apps (editors, terminals, browsers, daily-driver tools).
41	   Examples: Cursor, VSCode, Chrome, Signal, 1Password, Slack.
42	2. **Flatpak (Flathub)** — clean sandbox, cross-distro friendly, faster
43	   to launch than Snap, auto-update via `flatpak update`. Right when
44	   `.deb` is missing or vendor only publishes on Flathub. Default
45	   recommendation for community-packaged apps that need confinement.
46	3. **Snap** — set-and-forget auto-refresh via `snapd` (4×/day, no user
47	   action). Acceptable for non-hot-path apps where the extra ~1-3s
48	   startup penalty is invisible (password manager, music player).
49	   Avoid for hot-path apps; the daily startup cost adds up.
50	4. **AppImage + AppImageLauncher** — when 1-3 are unavailable. No
51	   auto-update unless the bundle ships `.zsync` AND AppImageLauncher's
52	   update check is configured. Re-running our ansible task is the
53	   typical refresh path.
54	5. **Cargo / from-source / tarball** — last resort. Manual everything,
55	   no apt/snap/flatpak update path. Only when upstream really only
56	   ships source.
57	
58	> **Why not "always Snap"?** Snap looks similar to Homebrew Cask on
59	> macOS but the comparison is misleading. Snap apps live in
60	> `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` mounted as squashfs and bring up an AppArmor
61	> sandbox on every launch — Firefox snap takes ~2-3s to boot on SSD
62	> versus ~0.3s for the `.deb`. The sandbox also breaks subtle workflows
63	> by default (snap Bitwarden can't read `~/.ssh` without `snap connect
64	> bitwarden:password-manager-service`; many snaps can't see external
65	> drives). For occasional-use apps these costs are invisible; for
66	> daily drivers (browser, IDE, terminal) they're a real annoyance.
67	> Snap is *fine* — it's just not the universal answer macOS users
68	> sometimes assume from their Cask experience. Pick by row 1-3 above.
69	
70	## Inventory of GUI apps on this machine
71	
72	### Ansible-managed (this repo)
73	
74	| App | Mechanism | Auto-update? | Source-of-truth | Where it lives |
75	|---|---|---|---|---|
76	| **Cursor** | `.deb` (auto-adds `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources`) | ✅ `apt upgrade cursor` | [`gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) "Install Cursor via .deb" | `/usr/share/cursor/` |
77	| **VSCode** | `.deb` (auto-adds `vscode.sources`) | ✅ `apt upgrade code` | same role | `/usr/share/code/` |
78	| **Discord** | `flatpak` (default, recommended) OR `.deb` (no apt source) — picked by `discordChannel` chezmoi prompt | ✅ via `flatpak update` (default) / ❌ manual on `.deb` | same role | `~/.local/share/flatpak/app/com.discordapp.Discord/` (flatpak) or `/usr/share/discord/` (.deb) |
79	| **Zen Browser** | AppImage at `~/Applications/zen.AppImage` (stable filename, no version suffix) | ❌ — re-run ansible task | same role | `~/Applications/zen.AppImage` |
80	| **Alacritty** | `cargo install alacritty` | ❌ — `just upgrade-cargo` | [`devtools` role](../../dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml) | `~/.cargo/bin/alacritty` |
81	| **AppImageLauncher** | `.deb` (PPA on 22.04, GitHub release on 24.04) | ✅ via apt | same role | system + `appimagelauncherd.service` (user) |
82	| **Bitwarden CLI** (`bw`) | npm via mise (gated by `installBitwarden=true`) | ❌ — `just upgrade-mise` | [`bitwarden` role](../../dot_ansible/roles/bitwarden/tasks/main.yml) | `~/.local/share/mise/...` |
83	| **Bitwarden Desktop** | Snap (`bitwarden`) → `.deb` fallback if `snap` unavailable; gated by `installBitwarden=true` AND `profile=ubuntu_desktop` | ✅ via `snapd` background refresh (or `apt upgrade` for fallback `.deb`) | same role | `/snap/bitwarden/current/` |
84	
85	### Manually managed (you installed these yourself, outside ansible)
86	
87	| App | Mechanism | Auto-update? | How it got there | How to upgrade |
88	|---|---|---|---|---|
89	| **Spotify** | Snap (publisher `Spotify**`) | ✅ background | Ubuntu App Center | `snap refresh spotify` |
90	| **Firefox** | Snap (canonical default since Ubuntu 22.04) | ✅ background | preinstalled with the OS | `snap refresh firefox` |
91	| **btop** | Snap (kz6fittycent) | ✅ background | manual | `snap refresh btop` |
92	| **Frpc Desktop** | AppImage at `~/Applications/Frpc-Desktop-1.2.1.AppImage` | ❌ — manual re-download | manual drop-in | overwrite the file |
93	| **Clash for Windows** | tarball at `~/Documents/ClashForWindows/` ⚠️ | ❌ **DEPRECATED upstream** | extracted manually 2025 | **Migrate** — see below |
94	
95	> **Clash for Windows is dead.** The original developer (Fndroid)
96	> publicly stopped maintenance in **2023-11** and the GitHub repo is
97	> archived. No new releases, no CVE patches. Migrate to one of the
98	> maintained forks:
99	>
100	> - [Clash Verge Rev](https://github.com/clash-verge-rev/clash-verge-rev) — active fork, ships .deb + AppImage
101	> - [Clash Nyanpasu](https://github.com/libnyanpasu/clash-nyanpasu) — Tauri-based GUI, AppImage + .deb
102	> - [Mihomo Party](https://github.com/mihomo-party-org/mihomo-party) — successor of CFW UX, AppImage + .deb
103	>
104	> All three publish `.deb` packages — drop the new app into `gui_apps_linux`
105	> following the [`.deb` pattern](#concrete-patterns) below and delete
106	> `~/Documents/ClashForWindows/` after the new one is wired up.
107	
108	## Why `.deb` auto-update works (the apt-source postinst trick)
109	
110	When `dpkg -i cursor_<v>_amd64.deb` runs, Cursor's package contains a
111	`DEBIAN/postinst` script that, on success, writes:
112	
113	- `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources` — pointing at `https://downloads.cursor.com/aptrepo`
114	- `/usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg` — the signing key
115	
116	After that, `apt update` pulls Cursor's release index alongside Ubuntu's
117	own, and `apt upgrade cursor` (or generic `apt upgrade` / `just upgrade-system`)
118	treats it like any other apt package. The user never needs to revisit
119	cursor.com.
120	
121	You can verify this for any installed `.deb`:
122	
123	```sh
124	dpkg -L cursor | grep -E 'sources|keyring'
125	# /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources
126	# /usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg
127	```
128	
129	VSCode, Chrome, Signal, 1Password, Slack, Microsoft Edge, Brave all
130	follow this pattern. **Discord does not** — see the next section.
```

cliphist_search() {
  if command -v maccy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # macOS Maccy backend
    maccy-history-search "$@"
  elif command -v copyq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Linux CopyQ backend
    copyq-history-search "$@"
  else
    echo "No supported clipboard manager found" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

# Cross-platform clipboard-history helper — hybrid (Maccy on mac + CopyQ on Linux)

## Context

A previous helper at `dot_config/shell/56_raycast_clipboard.sh.tmpl` exposed `rcb`/`rcbl`/`rcbe` to query Raycast's clipboard history. Raycast 1.7+ moved to SQLCipher with a key derivation that cannot be recovered from the keychain without binary reverse-engineering. The helper was deleted 2026-05; the post-mortem lives at [`pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md`](../../pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md).

The user wants a *queryable* clipboard-history workflow with a unified shell API (`cb` / `cbl` / `cbe`) that works the same on macOS and Ubuntu desktop, so muscle memory carries across hosts. `ubuntu_server` (no display server) should gracefully no-op with a hint.

## Decision: hybrid backend, unified API

Different tool per OS, single shell helper dispatches by backend detection:

| OS | Tool | Install | Has CLI? |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS | **Maccy** | `brew install --cask maccy` (signed, healthy on brew, `auto_updates`, macOS 14+) | No — query plaintext SQLite |
| Ubuntu desktop | **CopyQ** | `sudo apt install copyq` (stock 22.04 / 24.04 repos) | Yes — `copyq read/select/eval` |
| Ubuntu server | none | skip | n/a |

**Why hybrid, not CopyQ-everywhere**: the CopyQ Homebrew cask is deprecated (disabled 2026-09-01) — not the upstream project, only the cask, because `CopyQ.app` isn't signed for macOS Gatekeeper (upstream issue [hluk/CopyQ#3498](https://github.com/hluk/CopyQ/issues/3498)). CopyQ on Linux is unaffected and remains the canonical pick. Maccy is the most maintained signed-and-on-brew clipboard manager for macOS; trade-off is no shipped CLI, so the helper queries Maccy's plaintext SQLite directly.

**Coexistence with Raycast** (per user choice): both Raycast and Maccy will record every Cmd+C on macOS in parallel. No functional conflict — storage duplication only. Manual disable of Raycast's clipboard module is optional and not part of this change.

## File changes

### 1. macOS install — `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`

Add one line under "Casks - System Utilities" (existing section, no Jinja2 gate — Maccy is small, useful on every mac, signed, auto-updating):

\```
cask "maccy"                       # Plaintext-SQLite clipboard history (scriptable)
\```

### 3. Shell helper — `dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh`

New file (plain `.sh`, **not** `.sh.tmpl` — uses runtime backend detection, no chezmoi vars). POSIX subset, both shells source. Slot 56 reused (the deleted Raycast helper occupied it).

**Public API:**

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `cbl [N]` | List recent N items (default 20), tab-separated `<index>\t<first-line-preview>` |
| `cb` | fzf picker → copy selected item to system clipboard (moves to top of stack) |
| `cbe` | fzf picker → edit selection in `$EDITOR` → write back as a new clip |

**Backend dispatch** (`_clip_backend` internal helper):

- Manual override: `CLIP_BACKEND=maccy` or `CLIP_BACKEND=copyq` env var skips autodetect.
- macOS autodetect order: Maccy (probe SQLite paths) → CopyQ (if installed manually).
- Linux autodetect order: CopyQ (`command -v copyq` + `copyq size` to verify daemon is up).
- No backend found → one-line install hint to stderr, returns non-zero. The hint is the same install command from §1 / §2.

**Maccy SQLite path probe** (handles both sandbox modes):
1. `$HOME/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite` (brew cask, non-sandboxed)
2. `$HOME/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite` (Mac App Store, sandboxed)

**CopyQ backend internals:**
- `cbl` → `copyq eval` with a small JS loop printing `i\tread(i).split("\n")[0]\n` for `i < min(size(), N)`.
- `cb` → `copyq select <idx>` (atomic: moves to top of stack + writes to system clipboard).
- `cbe` → `copyq read <idx>` → tempfile → `$EDITOR` → `copyq copy - < tmpfile`.

**Maccy backend internals** (Core Data tables — see Verification §3 below for the required schema-confirmation step):
- `cbl` → `sqlite3` JOIN of `ZHISTORYITEM` + `ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT`, filter on `ZTYPE = 'public.utf8-plain-text'`, ORDER BY `ZFIRSTCOPIEDAT DESC`, LIMIT N.
- `cb` → SELECT `ZVALUE` by Z_PK → pipe to `pbcopy`. Maccy will re-record the clip at top of stack (acceptable side effect — adds a duplicate at index 0, not a bug).
- `cbe` → same as `cb` but via tempfile + `$EDITOR`.

Tier: **shared** per CLAUDE.md "three-tier file placement" — POSIX only, no ZLE widgets / `bindkey` / `setopt` / `compdef`. Both shells source it.

  - `cbl` / function / `dot_config/shell/56_clipboard_history.sh` / list recent N clipboard items

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Cross-platform clipboard-history helper — hybrid (Maccy on mac + CopyQ on Linux)

## Context

A previous helper at `dot_config/shell/56_raycast_clipboard.sh.tmpl` exposed `rcb`/`rcbl`/`rcbe` to query Raycast's clipboard history. Raycast 1.7+ moved to SQLCipher with a key derivation that cannot be recovered from the keychain without binary reverse-engineering. The helper was deleted 2026-05; the post-mortem lives at [`pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md`](../../pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md).

The user wants a *queryable* clipboard-history workflow with a unified shell API (`cb` / `cbl` / `cbe`) that works the same on macOS and Ubuntu desktop, so muscle memory carries across hosts. `ubuntu_server` (no display server) should gracefully no-op with a hint.

## Decision: hybrid backend, unified API

Different tool per OS, single shell helper dispatches by backend detection:

| OS | Tool | Install | Has CLI? |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS | **Maccy** | `brew install --cask maccy` (signed, healthy on brew, `auto_updates`, macOS 14+) | No — query plaintext SQLite |
| Ubuntu desktop | **CopyQ** | `sudo apt install copyq` (stock 22.04 / 24.04 repos) | Yes — `copyq read/select/eval` |
| Ubuntu server | none | skip | n/a |

**Why hybrid, not CopyQ-everywhere**: the CopyQ Homebrew cask is deprecated (disabled 2026-09-01) — not the upstream project, only the cask, because `CopyQ.app` isn't signed for macOS Gatekeeper (upstream issue [hluk/CopyQ#3498](https://github.com/hluk/CopyQ/issues/3498)). CopyQ on Linux is unaffected and remains the canonical pick. Maccy is the most maintained signed-and-on-brew clipboard manager for macOS; trade-off is no shipped CLI, so the helper queries Maccy's plaintext SQLite directly.

**Coexistence with Raycast** (per user choice): both Raycast and Maccy will record every Cmd+C on macOS in parallel. No functional conflict — storage duplication only. Manual disable of Raycast's clipboard module is optional and not part of this change.

### 1. macOS install — `dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`

Add one line under "Casks - System Utilities" (existing section, no Jinja2 gate — Maccy is small, useful on every mac, signed, auto-updating):

```

```text
1	# Clipboard & OSC 52
2	
3	This doc explains how clipboard sync is wired across this dotfiles setup, with a focus on **OSC 52** — the escape sequence that lets a remote SSH session put text on your **local** machine's clipboard.
4	
5	## TL;DR
6	
7	| You are… | Yank in Neovim goes to… | Capture pane (`prefix+y/Y/C-y`) goes to… |
8	|----------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
9	| Local (macOS or Linux desktop) | system clipboard (default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`) | same, via `tmux load-buffer -w -` which emits OSC 52 *and* sets tmux's paste buffer |
10	| SSH (remote box, with or without tmux) | **local** machine's clipboard (via OSC 52) | **local** machine's clipboard (via tmux → OSC 52) |
11	
12	No extra tools, no X forwarding, no socat listener needed. The only hard requirement is a terminal emulator on your **local** machine that supports OSC 52 (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm — all do).
13	
14	## What is OSC 52?
15	
16	`OSC 52` is an ANSI escape sequence:
17	
18	```
19	ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64-of-data> BEL
20	```
21	
22	Any program that can write to a terminal can emit this sequence; the terminal emulator on the other end decodes the base64 and writes it to the system clipboard. The crucial property: **escape sequences travel up the TTY back to the client terminal**, so this works transparently over SSH, mosh, and nested `tmux ssh` chains — no display server, no socket forwarding.
23	
24	Tradeoffs:
25	
26	- **Write** is ubiquitous. Most modern terminals allow it by default or with a simple opt-in.
27	- **Read** (paste from local clipboard back into remote apps) is much less supported — many terminals refuse for obvious security reasons (a malicious server could exfiltrate your clipboard). Ghostty prompts; Alacritty flat-out ignores it.
28	- A terminal multiplexer (tmux, screen, zellij) sits between the inner app and the outer terminal. It must be configured to either **emit** OSC 52 to its host terminal or **pass through** OSC 52 from inner apps.
29	
30	Reference: [tmux Clipboard wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Clipboard), [XTerm control sequences (OSC)](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html).
31	
32	## How this repo wires it up
33	
34	Four layers cooperate. Removing any one silently breaks remote-clipboard sync.
35	
36	### 1. Terminal emulator (outer, on your local machine)
37	
38	Must accept OSC 52 writes from whatever is running inside it.
39	
40	**Ghostty / cmux** — [`dot_config/ghostty/config`](../../dot_config/ghostty/config):
41	
42	```conf
43	clipboard-write = allow   # let inner apps set the system clipboard
44	clipboard-read  = ask     # prompt before reads (safer default)
45	```
46	
47	Both match current Ghostty defaults but are pinned explicitly so policy drifts from upstream don't silently break (or weaken) this chain.
48	
49	**Alacritty** — native support, no config needed. Paste from OSC 52 not supported.
50	
51	**iTerm2 / Kitty / WezTerm** — native support. iTerm2 requires `Preferences → General → Selection → Applications in terminal may access clipboard` for reads.
52	
53	### 2. Multiplexer — tmux
54	
55	[`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf):
56	
57	```tmux
58	set -g set-clipboard on
59	
60	set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
61	set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
62	set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
63	
64	set -g allow-passthrough on
65	```
66	
67	- **`set-clipboard on`** — tmux both re-emits OSC 52 to the outer terminal when its own copy-mode yanks, and passes OSC 52 from inner apps (Neovim, less, etc.) through. `external` would only pass through; `on` is a strict superset and simpler.
68	- **`terminal-features …:clipboard`** — tells tmux the outer terminal supports OSC 52 without needing a terminfo `Ms` capability. Many distros ship a `tmux-256color` entry that lacks `Ms`, so declaring the feature directly avoids surprises when `chezmoi apply` is run on a fresh box.
69	- **`allow-passthrough on`** — lets terminal-image protocols (sixel, kitty graphics) work; also covers OSC passthrough for nested multiplexers.
70	
71	**Capture-pane helpers** — [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) — use the tmux-native idiom rather than shelling out:
72	
73	```tmux
74	bind y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p   | tmux load-buffer -w -"
75	bind Y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w -"
76	bind C-y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux … | tmux load-buffer -w -"
77	```
78	
79	`load-buffer -w -` reads stdin into tmux's paste buffer *and* (because of `-w`) forwards to the system clipboard via OSC 52. Previously these bindings used a `pbcopy | xclip | xsel` fallback chain that only worked locally — over SSH they copied to the **remote** machine's clipboard, which is useless. The tmux-native form works identically in both places.
80	
81	`set-buffer -w …` offers the same `-w` flag but takes data as an argument, which introduces shell-quoting landmines on multi-line pane content; `load-buffer -w -` reads stdin and sidesteps that.
82	
83	### 3. Editor — Neovim
84	
85	[`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua):
86	
87	```lua
88	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
89	
90	if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
91	  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
92	  vim.g.clipboard = {
93	    name = "OSC 52",
94	    copy  = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"),  ["*"] = osc52.copy("*")  },
95	    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
96	  }
97	end
98	```
99	
100	- Locally, LazyVim's default provider is used (`pbcopy`/`xclip`/`wl-copy` — with working paste).
101	- Over SSH, Neovim's built-in `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` (shipping since Neovim 0.10) emits OSC 52 directly, bypassing any `pbcopy` binary on the remote host.
102	- The check is `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — either is set by `sshd` for an interactive session.
103	
104	Why conditional rather than always-on OSC 52? OSC 52 paste is unreliable (see the terminal table above). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves Neovim's paste behaviour; the override only activates when `pbcopy` on the remote is clearly the wrong answer.
105	
106	### 4. Shell CLI — `x` (cross-platform clipboard wrapper)
107	
108	[`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x) (deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/x`) is a Bash wrapper with three subcommands:
109	
110	```bash
111	printf "hello" | x copy        # copy stdin to clipboard
112	x copy path/to/file            # copy file contents
113	x paste                        # print clipboard to stdout
114	x open https://example.com     # open URL/file in default app
115	```
116	
117	Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available.
118	
119	The OSC 52 fallback in `x` is also wrapped for tmux:
120	
121	```bash
122	if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
123	  printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
124	else
125	  printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
126	fi
127	```
128	
129	The `DCS tmux; ... ST` wrapper is tmux's passthrough escape — it tells tmux "hand this sequence to the outer terminal as-is", needed because tmux otherwise intercepts OSC 52.
130	
131	## Verifying the chain works
132	
133	On the remote box where Neovim yank is misbehaving, run:
134	
135	```bash
136	# tmux: does it believe the terminal can accept OSC 52?
137	tmux info | grep -Ei 'clipboard|Ms:'
138	# expect: clipboard: true  and an Ms entry that is NOT [missing]
139	
140	# shell: can x copy reach the clipboard?
141	printf "hello from %s" "$(hostname)" | x copy
142	# then Cmd+V / Ctrl+V into a local app → should paste "hello from <remote-host>"
143	
144	# Neovim: which provider is active?
145	nvim -c ':checkhealth provider.clipboard' -c ':only'
146	# expect: OSC 52 under SSH, native under local
147	```
148	
149	If `tmux info` shows `clipboard: false` after editing `common.conf`, remember a running tmux server **keeps its old capability table** — `tmux kill-server` (losing sessions; `tmux-resurrect` can restore them) and re-attach.
150	
151	## Common failure modes
152	
153	| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
154	|---------|-------------|-----|
155	| Yank works outside tmux but vanishes inside tmux (remote) | `set-clipboard off` or server running pre-edit binary | `tmux show -g set-clipboard`; `tmux kill-server` |
156	| `tmux info` shows `Ms: [missing]` | tmux's TERM entry lacks `Ms` *and* no `terminal-features …:clipboard` declared | already handled by [`common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf); on an unusual outer `$TERM`, add another `set -as terminal-features` line |
157	| Ghostty asks about clipboard every yank | `clipboard-read = ask`; Ghostty interprets some writes as reads when apps immediately re-fetch | switch to `clipboard-read = allow` if you trust everything inside your sessions |
158	| Neovim yank works, but `"*p` does nothing over SSH | paste over OSC 52 not supported by outer terminal | expected — use mouse middle-click or re-type; don't fight it |
159	| `prefix+y` still copies to remote clipboard | shim binary `tmux` resolves to an old pre-`load-buffer -w` version | `tmux -V` must be ≥ 3.3 for `load-buffer -w`; this repo enforces ≥ 3.3 via ansible `devtools` role |
160	| Nested tmux (`tmux inside ssh inside tmux`) | inner tmux eats OSC 52 | inner tmux needs `set -g allow-passthrough on`; already on in this config. Double-nested cases may require `Ptmux;…` wrapping |
161	
162	## Design notes / non-defaults
163	
164	- **tmux `set-clipboard`** is `on`, not `external`. `external` disables tmux's own OSC 52 emission from copy-mode; `on` is a superset and keeps `prefix+[` → `y` working.
165	- **Neovim OSC 52 provider** is gated on `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` rather than always-on, specifically so local paste (`"+p`) continues to work. If you primarily work over SSH and don't mind the paste tradeoff, the `if …` block can be removed.
166	- **`x` CLI ordering** prefers local backends (`pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, etc.) over OSC 52. This is intentional: when `pbcopy` is available, it's faster, doesn't touch the TTY, and works for very large payloads (OSC 52 payloads are size-limited by the terminal — iTerm2 caps at 1 MB, many others at 64-256 KB).
167	
168	## Related docs
169	
170	- [tmux](./tmux/README.md) — "OSC 52 Clipboard (SSH-friendly yank)" section
171	- [Ghostty](./ghostty.md) — terminal-side notes
172	- [`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`](../../dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x) — the `x` wrapper source
173	
174	## External references
175	
176	- [tmux Clipboard wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Clipboard)
177	- [Neovim `:help clipboard-osc52`](https://neovim.io/doc/user/provider.html#clipboard-osc52)
178	- [XTerm OSC 52 spec](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h3-Operating-System-Commands)
179
```
</details></tool-use>

1	---
2	# =============================================================================
3	# gui_apps_linux — Ubuntu/Debian desktop GUI app installer
4	#
5	# Handles the "desktop-only" category of apps that aren't in the apt default
6	# repos: Alacritty (cargo), AppImageLauncher (PPA / .deb / Lite), VSCode
7	# (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (.deb with graceful fallback), Discord (.deb,
8	# x86_64-only), Zen Browser (AppImage + .desktop), libfuse2 (AppImage runtime
9	# on Ubuntu 22.04+), and a placeholder hook for Antigravity once an official
10	# Linux package ships.
11	#
12	# No-op on:
13	#   - macOS  → Brewfile (`cask "alacritty"`, `cask "visual-studio-code"` when
14	#              you add them) covers the desktop story. This role emits a
15	#              debug note only on Darwin, no install logic runs.
16	#   - armhf  → 32-bit ARM has no practical GUI story; cargo builds are slow
17	#              and AppImages lack first-class armv7 support.
18	#   - noRoot → `--skip-tags sudo` (set by run_onchange) skips every system
19	#              apt/deb/PPA task. AppImageLauncher Lite (user-level AppImage)
20	#              still runs when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true` is passed via
21	#              `--extra-vars`.
22	#
23	# Editor user-config overlays (settings.json / keybindings.json) are handled
24	# by chezmoi itself, NOT ansible — see `.chezmoitemplates/editor/` and the
25	# `modify_settings.json.tmpl` / `create_keybindings.json.tmpl` source files.
26	#
27	# Adding a new GUI app: read docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md FIRST. It
28	# contains the .deb / Snap / Flatpak / AppImage decision tree, the
29	# "concrete patterns" you'd copy here, and the inventory table you must
30	# also update so the doc stays in sync with this role.
31	# =============================================================================
32

All three functions print to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`) AND copy to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge. Shell-level counterparts of the `prefix + M-y` / `M-i` tmux bindings — see [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 133](../tools/tmux/README.md#osc-133-command-boundary-navigation-warp-style).

Reuses the AI Capture agent fallback (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent); 10-min cached in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/`. `-d` includes the visible area of each session's active pane (20-100 lines, self-capture skipped); set `TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1` in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` to make `-d` implicit (override with `--shallow`). `--sort closability` orders keep → check → safe (default: alphabetical); `--only {safe,check,keep}` filters to one tier. `-r` bypasses cache; `-i` opens fzf picker that switches client on Enter (also reachable via tmux `prefix + Space → Sessions → AI session summary`); `--dry-run` prints the prompt without calling the LLM. **On hosts with multiple tmux binaries** (apt + appimage, brew + system) export `TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/path/to/tmux` so tsum talks to the right server. |

662	
663	> One-shot pipeline: capture a past block (via `cpblock N`) and pass it to a coding-agent CLI (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent) in non-interactive / advisory mode. Agent auto-detected in the order listed; override with `-a AGENT`. Prompt override via `-p PROMPT`. Agent reply goes to stdout (pipe-friendly: `aifix | tee /tmp/advice.md`), status line to stderr.

```text
---
# Bitwarden role - CLI installation + Desktop app (for SSH agent)
# CLI: Installs @bitwarden/cli via npm, with mise fallback when npm is not in PATH.
# Desktop: Installs Bitwarden desktop app (snap/deb on Linux, Homebrew cask on macOS)
#          when bitwarden_install_desktop=true (passed via --extra-vars)

# =============================================================================
# CLI Installation
# =============================================================================

- name: Check if Bitwarden CLI is already installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Darwin", "Debian"]
  ansible.builtin.command: which bw
  register: bitwarden_cli_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Check if npm is available for Bitwarden CLI install
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Darwin", "Debian"]
    - bitwarden_cli_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.command: npm --version
  register: bitwarden_npm_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

# Prefer mise's npm: system npm on noRoot Linux hosts has prefix /usr/local
# (unwritable without sudo). mise's user-managed prefix works without sudo on
# both Linux and macOS.
- name: Check for user-installed mise (Bitwarden)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Darwin", "Debian"]
    - bitwarden_cli_check.rc != 0
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/mise"
  register: bitwarden_mise_user_bin

- name: Set Bitwarden mise binary path (user install)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Darwin", "Debian"]
    - bitwarden_cli_check.rc != 0
    - bitwarden_mise_user_bin.stat.exists | default(false)
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    bitwarden_mise_bin: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/mise"

- name: Check for system mise (Bitwarden)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Darwin", "Debian"]
    - bitwarden_cli_check.rc != 0
    - bitwarden_mise_bin is not defined
  ansible.builtin.command: mise --version
  register: bitwarden_mise_system_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Set Bitwarden mise binary path (system install)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Darwin", "Debian"]
    - bitwarden_cli_check.rc != 0
    - bitwarden_mise_bin is not defined
```
</details></tool-use>

```sh
# 56_clipboard_history.sh — cross-platform clipboard-history helpers.
#
# Wraps Maccy (macOS, plaintext SQLite) and CopyQ (Linux, shipped CLI) behind
# a unified `cb` / `cbl` / `cbe` API. Replaces the Raycast-specific helper
# deleted in 2026-05 — Raycast 1.7+ encrypts its DB with SQLCipher and the
# key cannot be recovered without binary RE; see
# pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md.
#
# Backend selection (override autodetect with CLIP_BACKEND=copyq|maccy):
#   macOS:  prefer Maccy SQLite, fall back to CopyQ if installed manually.
#   Linux:  CopyQ only.
# No backend → one-line install hint to stderr (ubuntu_server typical case).
#
# Maccy schema (verified against p0deje/Maccy@master HistoryItem.swift +
# HistoryItemContent.swift, 2026-05):
#   ZHISTORYITEM(Z_PK, ZAPPLICATION, ZFIRSTCOPIEDAT, ZLASTCOPIEDAT,
#                ZNUMBEROFCOPIES, ZPIN, ZTITLE)
#   ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT(Z_PK, ZTYPE, ZVALUE, ZITEM -> ZHISTORYITEM.Z_PK)
# Core Data dates are seconds since 2001-01-01; add 978307200 for Unix epoch.

# ---- backend detection -----------------------------------------------------

_clip_maccy_path() {
    p="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
    p="$HOME/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
    return 1
}

_clip_copyq_ready() {
    command -v copyq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    copyq size >/dev/null 2>&1
}

_clip_backend() {
    case "${CLIP_BACKEND:-}" in
        copyq) _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq ;;
        maccy) _clip_maccy_path ;;
        '')
            if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
                _clip_maccy_path && return 0
                _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq
            else
                _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq
            fi
            ;;
        *)
            printf 'clipboard-history: unknown CLIP_BACKEND=%s (expected: copyq|maccy)\n' "$CLIP_BACKEND" >&2
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
}

_clip_hint() {
    cat >&2 <<'HINT'
clipboard-history: no backend found.

  macOS:  brew install --cask maccy   (then launch once from Spotlight)
  Linux:  sudo apt install copyq      (autostarts on next X session)

See docs/tools/clipboard.md → Clipboard History.
HINT
}

_clip_is_uint() {
    case "$1" in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac
}

# ---- cbl: list recent N items (tab-separated <idx>\t<first-line>) ----------

cbl() {
    n=${1:-20}
    if ! _clip_is_uint "$n"; then
        echo "cbl: argument must be a positive integer (got: $n)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    b=$(_clip_backend) || { _clip_hint; return 1; }
    case "$b" in
        copyq)
            copyq eval "
                var n = Math.min(size(), $n);
                for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                    var line = read(i).split('\n')[0];
                    if (line.length > 0) print(i + '\t' + line + '\n');
                }
            "
            ;;
        maccy:*)
            db=${b#maccy:}
            sqlite3 -readonly -batch "$db" <<SQL
.mode tabs
.headers off
SELECT Z.Z_PK,
       substr(replace(CAST(C.ZVALUE AS TEXT), char(10), ' '), 1, 200)
FROM ZHISTORYITEM Z
JOIN ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT C ON C.ZITEM = Z.Z_PK
WHERE C.ZTYPE = 'public.utf8-plain-text'
ORDER BY Z.ZLASTCOPIEDAT DESC
LIMIT $n;
SQL
            ;;
    esac
}

# ---- cb: fzf-pick a clip → copy to system clipboard ------------------------

cb() {
    command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "cb: fzf not found" >&2; return 1; }
    b=$(_clip_backend) || { _clip_hint; return 1; }
    sel=$(cbl 100 | fzf --no-multi --with-nth=2.. --delimiter='	' --prompt='clip> ') || return 1
    idx=$(printf '%s\n' "$sel" | cut -f1)
    _clip_is_uint "$idx" || { echo "cb: bad index from fzf: $idx" >&2; return 1; }
    case "$b" in
        copyq)
            copyq select "$idx"
            ;;
        maccy:*)
            db=${b#maccy:}
            sqlite3 -readonly -batch "$db" \
                "SELECT CAST(ZVALUE AS TEXT) FROM ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT \
                 WHERE ZITEM=$idx AND ZTYPE='public.utf8-plain-text' LIMIT 1;" \
                | pbcopy
            ;;
    esac
}

# ---- cbe: fzf-pick → edit in $EDITOR → write back to clipboard -------------

cbe() {
    command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "cbe: fzf not found" >&2; return 1; }
    b=$(_clip_backend) || { _clip_hint; return 1; }
    sel=$(cbl 100 | fzf --no-multi --with-nth=2.. --delimiter='	' --prompt='cb-edit> ') || return 1
    idx=$(printf '%s\n' "$sel" | cut -f1)
    _clip_is_uint "$idx" || { echo "cbe: bad index from fzf: $idx" >&2; return 1; }
    tmp=$(mktemp -t clipedit.XXXXXX) || return 1
    case "$b" in
        copyq)
            copyq read "$idx" > "$tmp"
            ;;
        maccy:*)
            db=${b#maccy:}
            sqlite3 -readonly -batch "$db" \
                "SELECT CAST(ZVALUE AS TEXT) FROM ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT \
                 WHERE ZITEM=$idx AND ZTYPE='public.utf8-plain-text' LIMIT 1;" \
                > "$tmp"
            ;;
    esac
    ${EDITOR:-nvim} "$tmp"
    if [ -s "$tmp" ]; then
        case "$b" in
            copyq)  copyq copy - < "$tmp" ;;
            maccy:*) pbcopy < "$tmp" ;;
        esac
    fi
    rm -f "$tmp"
}
